record.original_question: Algebraic Multigrid Analysis for Theoretical Computer Scientists: Show that for polynomially bounded SWCDDM matrices $M$, Algebraic Multigrid runs in time $~O(nnz(M))$ to compute an (implicitly represented) symmetric matrix $Z$, which can be applied in $O(nnz(M))$ time, and satisfies the condition that $ Omega(1) M^-1 Z O(1) M^-1$. In particular, the constants are independent of the problem size $n$.

evidence.quote: Show that for polynomially bounded SWCDDM matrices $\mathbf{M}$, Algebraic Multigrid runs in time $\tilde{O}(\operatorname{nnz}(\mathbf{M}))$ to compute an (implicitly represented) symmetric matrix $\mathbf{Z}$, which can be applied in $O(\operatorname{nnz}(\mathbf{M}))$ time, and satisfies the condition that $ \Omega(1) \mathbf{M}^{-1} \preceq \mathbf{Z} \preceq O(1) \mathbf{M}^{-1}$. In particular, the constants are independent of the problem size $n$.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\mathbf{M} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ be a symmetric weakly column diagonally dominant M-matrix (SWCDDM); i.e., $\mathbf{M}$ is symmetric, all off-diagonal entries are nonpositive, all diagonal entries are positive, and for every column $j$ one has $\mathbf{M}_{jj} \ge \sum_{i \ne j} |\mathbf{M}_{ij}|$. Assume in addition that $\mathbf{M}$ is polynomially bounded, meaning that the ratio of the largest to smallest nonzero magnitudes among the entries of $\mathbf{M}$ is bounded by $\mathrm{poly}(n)$. Let $\mathrm{nnz}(\mathbf{M})$ denote the number of nonzero entries of $\mathbf{M}$. For symmetric positive (semi)definite matrices $\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{B}$, write $\mathbf{A} \preceq \mathbf{B}$ for the Loewner order, i.e. $\mathbf{B} - \mathbf{A}$ is positive semidefinite. The notation $\widetilde{O}(\cdot)$ hides factors polylogarithmic in $n$.

Problem. Prove that there is an Algebraic Multigrid algorithm that, given any such polynomially bounded SWCDDM matrix $\mathbf{M}$:
(i) runs in time $\widetilde{O}(\mathrm{nnz}(\mathbf{M}))$;
(ii) outputs an implicit representation of a symmetric matrix $\mathbf{Z}$ such that, for any vector $\mathbf{b} \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the product $\mathbf{Z}\mathbf{b}$ can be computed in $O(\mathrm{nnz}(\mathbf{M}))$ time;
(iii) produces $\mathbf{Z}$ satisfying the spectral approximation
$$\Omega(1)\,\mathbf{M}^{-1} \;\preceq\; \mathbf{Z} \;\preceq\; O(1)\,\mathbf{M}^{-1},$$
where the hidden constants are absolute and independent of $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: No direct evidence was found establishing or refuting an Algebraic Multigrid algorithm with the stated $\widetilde{O}(\mathrm{nnz}(\mathbf{M}))$ runtime and $O(1)$-spectral-approximation guarantee for polynomially bounded SWCDDM matrices, with constants independent of $n$. While nearly-linear-time SDD/Laplacian solvers (Spielman–Teng and successors) and AMG variants such as LAMG are known, the specific theoretical guarantee posed here for general AMG on this matrix class does not appear settled in the search results.

status_evidence.title: Lean Algebraic Multigrid (LAMG): Fast Graph Laplacian Linear Solver
status_evidence.snippet: LAMG solves graph Laplacian systems with empirically near-linear runtime and storage in the number of edges.
status_evidence.claim: AMG variants achieve empirical near-linear scaling for Laplacian systems, but theoretical worst-case guarantees of the form requested are not established here.

status_evidence.title: An Algebraic Multigrid Method with Guaranteed Convergence Rate
status_evidence.snippet: Provides AMG with guaranteed convergence rates for nonsingular symmetric M-matrices with nonnegative row sum.
status_evidence.claim: Guaranteed-rate AMG results exist for related M-matrix classes, but do not directly establish the stated nnz-time, O(1)-spectral-approximation theorem for polynomially bounded SWCDDM matrices.
